nodes.notes: Captures GitHub push events, performs triage and initial analysis, and creates analysis requests.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Levels the load and drives auto-scaling for the first Fargate cluster.

nodes.name: ECS Fargate
nodes.notes: Auto-scaling cluster that pulls messages from SQS, clones code into ephemeral storage, analyzes it, and pushes reports.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Hosts the API and UI; receives analysis reports from Fargate and serves results to developers.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.notes: Acts as a temporary storage queue for incoming reports and stores final processed analysis reports.

nodes.name: ECS Fargate
nodes.notes: Compute Engine component that polls Aurora for raw reports, computes code quality metrics, and outputs final reports.

nodes.name: ES
nodes.notes: In-house Elasticsearch service (not yet Amazon managed) used to store shared data in an optimized format for search.

edges.notes: Developers push code changes into a GitHub repo.
Code change triggers an event captured by Lambda.
Lambda does triage and sends an analysis request to the SQS queue.
Fargate cluster polls the SQS queue.
SQS provides the analysis request to Fargate.
Fargate requests to clone the code from GitHub.
Code is cloned into Fargate ephemeral storage.
Once analyzed, Fargate pushes the analysis report to the EC2 instance through an API.
EC2 stores the report into Aurora as temporary storage.
The Compute Engine (Fargate) polls the Aurora database to extract reports.
Raw report is extracted from Aurora by the Compute Engine.
After computing code quality metrics, the Compute Engine updates Aurora with the final analysis report.
Compute Engine also stores additional shared data in an optimized format in the in-house Elasticsearch.
Developers access the UI or call the API on EC2 to extract and view the analysis results.
